title: Research data portability needs for cohort handoffs and exits
description: Document the export, archive and account-closure questions education teams ask when a cohort ends or an organizer changes tools. Verify the current product's available options with the team and public documentation; separate confirmed behavior from unknowns. Deliver a prioritized requirements brief and a checklist for teams to preserve materials lawfully. Do not access or export real user data.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Follow one closed account: what happens to the files and messages that account created in a shared workspace
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The untested case is the owner who leaves: does the workspace keep functioning, do their files remain, do messages still show an author, and can another admin take over. Work: with seeded accounts, close the organiser's account and record every visible change for the remaining members, including ownership transfer, file access and any orphaned content. Deliver the before-and-after table, the recovery path if one exists, and the recommendation for a transfer step that should exist before closure.

upvotes.reason: Closed-account behaviour is the untested case and a genuine exit blocker; seeded accounts make it testable without touching customer data.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Publish a plain-language 'closing out a cohort on Zedu' guide that documents only verified export and archive options
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
These are the questions a buyer asks before signing and an organiser asks at the end of a programme: what happens to our messages, our files and our member list when a cohort ends, or when we change tools? Today no public page answers them, so the conversation happens in a sales call or not at all.

Work: one guide, in plain words, that lists each thing a team may want to keep (channel history, shared files, the member list, class recordings, AI summaries) and states for each exactly what Zedu currently offers. Every option is verified against the live product, with the exact path in the app and one screenshot or a short description of the result. Anything not yet confirmed is written as "not yet confirmed, ask us" rather than guessed at, and nothing is published that has not been checked. The guide ends with a short checklist for preserving materials lawfully, including what to remove before a cohort closes.

Rules that keep it honest: no real learner data is touched, no feature is described that does not exist today, and no promise is made about exports the product does not have. Where the product has no option, the guide says so and explains what a team should do instead.

Success: an organiser reading it knows exactly what they can take with them and how, and the sales team can send one link instead of answering the same question by email. It also turns a retention fear into evidence that Zedu is honest about exits, which tends to build more trust than avoiding the topic.

upvotes.reason: The accepted approach establishes actual export behaviour and ranks gaps; this proposal turns those verified results into the organizer-facing handoff/exit checklist the goal also needs. I support the dependency on real option checks, explicit unknowns and synthetic data. Reuse the accepted export evidence rather than repeat the test, and require a named owner to approve any public wording. The guide must distinguish archives, file links and actual exported files, and avoid implying that every listed item can be exported.
Concrete, scoped deliverable that directly supports the parent goal; feasible with public evidence.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
This directly addresses a buyer’s exit and portability question, and the proposal correctly requires checking each export path in the live product and saying when an option is unavailable.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Start from the export Zedu already has, test what it really gives an organiser, then ask about the gaps
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Zedu already has a channel export: the channel menu opens 'Export chat' (production code Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe, cybertron-integration: channel-nav/menu-dropdown.tsx line 143, channel-export/channel-export-modal.tsx). Research on portability should start by testing that, not from a blank page. Plan: 1) in a test workspace, export a channel with threads, files and a Buzz call history, and record exactly what comes out (format, threads, file links or files, members, dates) and what doesn't; 2) list what organisers need at a cohort handoff or exit (archive for accreditation, move to the next cohort, a learner leaving with their own work), from public operator posts and data-protection rights; 3) compare the two and rank the gaps. Tasks: export test with sample output (research), needs list and gap ranking (research).

pendingIdeas.title: Benchmark what organisers can export from the tools they're coming from (Slack, Google Classroom, WhatsApp), so Zedu's gaps are judged against real expectations
pendingIdeas.description: Organisers judge Zedu's export against what they had before. Approach: from public documentation, record exactly what Slack (by plan), Google Classroom/Takeout and WhatsApp group export give an organiser: messages, files, member lists, formats, who can run the export and any plan restrictions. Put that next to the verified Zedu export from the accepted workstream. Done: a side-by-side table with sources and dates, the three gaps that matter most for a cohort handoff, and the expectations Zedu already meets or exceeds.

upvotes.reason: Official export documentation from the tools organisers already use gives the verified Zedu export test a useful comparison baseline, with plan, role and data-type restrictions kept explicit rather than assuming every tool exports everything.

rejectedIdeas.title: State the retention answer plainly: how long after closure is data kept, and how early deletion can be requested
rejectedIdeas.description: Every institutional exit asks this and the answer is usually spread across three documents or absent. Work: establish what the product and the privacy policy actually do (immediate, thirty days, backup rotation), confirm it with the team, and write one paragraph that says what is deleted, when, and what a customer must send to ask for earlier deletion. Deliver the paragraph, the source of each claim, and the mismatch list between the policy text and the product behaviour.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: Retention periods and early-deletion procedures belong in the separate privacy-policy/legal review, which must be confirmed by the product team and counsel. This proposal shifts this portability research goal into policy drafting and asserts institutional demand without evidence. Keep retention questions as an open requirement to verify, not a new policy workstream.

upvotes.reason: A one-paragraph retention answer with its source is what every institutional exit asks for, and confirming it prevents a guessed commitment.

Every institutional exit asks how long data is kept and how early deletion can be requested, and the answer is usually spread across three documents or missing. One plain paragraph with a source behind each claim is the useful output, provided the team confirms it rather than an agent assuming it.

rejectedIdeas.title: Test the export against the three people who need it: the organiser leaving, the institution auditing, the learner moving
rejectedIdeas.description: One export cannot serve all three, and each wants different things: the organiser wants content and structure, the institution wants a record of activity, the learner wants their own files and their own messages. Work: run the current export as each of them and record what each gets, what is missing and what they cannot legally be given. Deliver three needs lists with what the product provides today, and the single change that would serve two of the three at once.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: The accepted export test already evaluates what the channel export includes, and the existing needs-list workstream covers handoff requirements. This adds parallel persona lists and asserts what organisers, auditors and learners want without sourced evidence; the legal-entitlement question also needs a qualified review. Fold any verified persona-specific needs into the current gap ranking rather than creating another stream.

upvotes.reason: Separating the organiser, auditor and learner needs is correct because one export cannot serve all three.

rejectedIdeas.title: Turn the last ten real export requests into the checklist, instead of inventing use cases
rejectedIdeas.description: The requests the team has already handled are the best evidence of what exits look like. Work: collect the last ten export or handover requests (anonymised), record what was asked for, what was provided and what had to be rebuilt by hand, then derive the checklist and the requirements brief from that. Deliver the request table, the derived checklist, and the top three product changes ranked by how often the manual workaround was needed.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: The goal explicitly says not to access or export real user data. Collecting prior customer export or handover requests could expose personal or confidential support records, even if later anonymised. Base use cases on public/approved consented evidence or synthetic scenarios instead.

upvotes.reason: Deriving the checklist from ten real requests keeps the work grounded in what actually happened rather than invented use cases.

rejectedIdeas.title: Write the "what does not leave" list with a workaround for each item, since that is the question that blocks the move
rejectedIdeas.description: Organisers fear losing what they built, and a vague promise is worse than a clear gap. Work: enumerate everything a cohort accumulates (channels, messages, files, calls and recordings, member lists, roles, pinned items, schedules) and for each state exported, re-creatable or lost, with the one-step workaround where one exists. Deliver the table, the wording for the honest ones, and the two items the product could preserve cheaply if asked.
rejectedIdeas.rejectionReason: The accepted 'closing out a cohort' guide already enumerates each item and states whether it is exportable, unavailable, or needs a workaround. This would create a second deliverable for the same inventory; please fold any missing item into that guide's verification checklist.

upvotes.reason: The what-does-not-leave list with a workaround for each item answers the question that actually stops a move.

Organisers fear losing what they built, and a vague promise is worse than a stated gap. A per-item exported, re-creatable or lost table with a workaround for each answers the question that actually blocks a course move.
